summary: Information from the test rows sneaks into training and the score lies.
headline: The answer key was in the room
overview: Leakage means the model saw something at training time that it will not have at prediction time. The score looks excellent and means nothing.
Here every label is a coin flip, so honest accuracy is 50%. Choose your features before splitting and cross-validation reports something much better.

break.label: Break it
break.explains: Pick the most useful-looking features using every row, then cross-validate. Pure noise now seems predictable.

check.question: Why does choosing features on the whole dataset before cross-validating inflate the score?
options: The test rows helped decide which features to keep

realLife: Scaling, imputing, selecting features and even PCA all learn from data, so every one of them belongs inside the training fold.
data: Sixty rows and 200 columns of random numbers, with random 0/1 labels. Ten features are chosen by their link to the label, then logistic regression is cross-validated over five folds. Twelve fresh draws are shown. The numbers vary by draw, which is why there are twelve.
maths: Honest: for each fold, pick features using training rows only.
Leaky: pick features using all rows, then split.
With 200 noise columns, some always look related to the labels by chance. Picking them with the test rows included keeps the lucky ones.
code:
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectKBest
pipe = make_pipeline(SelectKBest(k=10), LogisticRegression())
cross_val_score(pipe, X, y, cv=5)   # selection redone inside each fold

sources.title: scikit-learn: common pitfalls, data leakage
